text:
zara: hey folks, day 1 gotcha. installed Homebrew on M1 (/opt/homebrew), asdf for runtimes, and 1Password for SSH keys. most stuff works in terminal but when i open the repo in VS Code (from Finder) the integrated terminal shows the right python/node from asdf, but pre-commit hooks run by the editor still pick up /usr/bin/python and fail linting. any ideas?

oscar: welcome zara! this is usually an environment inheritance problem: apps launched from GUI (Finder/Spotlight/Dock) don't always get the same PATH as shells. VS Code launched that way spawns the language server / hooks from the environment that launchd provided.

mike: quick checks: run `env | grep -i asdf` and `which python` from the integrated terminal, then open a file, run a failing hook, and in the VS Code "Output" panel check the full command path for the hook. Also `type -a pre-commit` can show which binary is used.

zara: i ran those. integrated terminal `which python` -> ~/.asdf/shims/python. pre-commit output shows `/usr/bin/python3` though. i have a `.pre-commit-config.yaml` that doesn't set explicit language version.

oscar: pre-commit runs in the context of the tool that's executed by the editor. VS Code's git hooks extension might shell out using a non-login shell. Two fixes: 1) ensure asdf init is in `~/.zprofile` (login shells) so GUI-launched apps inherit it, or 2) pin the pre-commit hooks to a specific runtime by adding `additional_dependencies` or `language_version` in the hook config.

anya: another pragmatic approach: in your repo create a small `bin/activate-env` script that exports PATH with `~/.asdf/shims` first and have editor settings call that before running hooks. Example `bin/activate-env`: 
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
exec "$@"
```
and set the pre-commit `hooks` `entry` to `bin/activate-env pre-commit-runner ...` if you prefer repo-local fix.

zara: good ideas. i put minimal asdf lines into `~/.zprofile` and logged out/in, but still saw the editor use system python for some Git actions. i checked `launchctl getenv PATH` and it didn't include my asdf shims.

oscar: on mac, launchd reads env from the login session only at session start. After you change `~/.zprofile` you must log out/in or reboot for launchd to pick it up. Some folks run `launchctl setenv PATH "$PATH"` manually but that's brittle. Best to log out and back in.

mike: also check whether you have a VS Code setting that runs Git operations via the system git vs an installed git. `git.path` in settings can override. If the editor uses the system git, hooks it spawns will inherit that PATH. Set `git.path` to `/opt/homebrew/bin/git` if you want the brew git.

zara: ok logged out and back in. editor now picks up asdf python for hooks — pre-commit hooks run correctly. one more small thing: SSH agent via 1Password seems flaky with VS Code terminals started from spotlight. sometimes `ssh -T git@github.com` fails until i run `eval $(op signin --sh)` in terminal. any tips to avoid repeated signins?

anya: OP sessions are ephemeral by design (MFA). For SSH keys prefer the 1Password desktop app's SSH agent integration which exposes a standard SSH agent socket and persists keys across GUI sessions. Enable "Use 1Password SSH agent" in the app settings and set `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` export in `~/.zprofile` to the socket path if needed. Or use system keychain agent and `ssh-add -K` for persistent keys if your org allows.

mike: also ensure VS Code is launched after the 1Password agent is running. If you keep 1Password in the menubar and it's started at login, apps launched after login should see the agent. If not, add `export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=$(gpgconf --list-dirs agent-socket)` or the 1Password socket path to `~/.zprofile` depending on the agent.

zara: noted. last tiny oddity: i use gpg for commit signing. in terminal `git commit -S` opens pinentry and works, but commit signing fails when i sign from VS Code's source control commit box. gpg errors say "no pinentry".

oscar: VS Code may run git operations in a non-interactive environment and not have access to the GUI pinentry. Solutions: use pinentry-mac and point gpg-agent to it in `~/.gnupg/gpg-agent.conf` with `pinentry-program /opt/homebrew/bin/pinentry-mac`, then `gpgconf --kill gpg-agent`. Also ensure `GPG_TTY` is set in shell profiles: `export GPG_TTY=$(tty)` in `~/.zprofile` so terminal sessions get it. For GUI apps, pinentry-mac should show a dialog.

anya: another approach if pinentry is still flaky: use gpg-agent with ssh support and configure git to use `gpg --batch --yes --pinentry-mode=loopback` only if you understand the security tradeoffs. We usually recommend pinentry-mac for desktops.

zara: thanks all — moving pinentry config, added asdf + SSH_AUTH_SOCK to `~/.zprofile`, logged out/in, and both hooks and signing work from VS Code launched from Spotlight now. leaving a short note in my onboarding dotfiles about "log out/in after updating zprofile for GUI apps". :coffee: 

onboard-bot: Welcome @zara! Nice write-up. If you want, create a PR to https://redwood.internal/onboarding/dev-setup with your `~/.zprofile` snippet and well include it in the central guide. :sparkles:
